items.title: Engineering Manager (Agent Engine)
items.description: Perplexity is seeking an Engineering Manager to lead and grow our highly driven Agent Engine team. The Agent Engine team designs and builds powerful agentic experiences including Perplexity Computer https://www.perplexity.ai/computer, the Comet ecosystem, our Agent API, and more. In short, we build frontier intelligence systems for the world's most discerning users. As the engineering manager supporting the Agent Engine team, you'll bring AI expertise, sharp product intuition, and strong leadership and collaboration skills to advance the frontier of what agents can accomplish for our millions of devoted users. You'll lead, grow, and support a team in solving many open problems in AI, including: - Designing frontier agent harnesses and systems to perform high-stakes, mission-critical work for our users; - Leveraging action and decision models that determine, based on complex multimodal states, how to accomplish user-specified objectives; - Providing consistently excellent experiences across local execution, headless cloud, custom executors, and other environments through sound system design and flexible abstractions; - Developing permission architectures, payload classifiers, and other methods to implement secure-by-design agentic capabilities; - Designing optimal data representations and modes of interaction between agents and their environments; - and much, much more. RESPONSIBILITIES - Provide technical leadership across multiple layers of a rapidly growing product in the AI agents space. - Develop and leverage cutting-edge AI systems and related technologies to advance the capability frontier and scale those capabilities for a rapidly growing userbase. - Exercise sharp technical & product intuition to guide the team’s system architectures and product roadmaps. - Drive product reliability, code quality, AI evaluation, testing, and maintenance for the broader team. - Oversee hiring, onboarding, and mentorship for a rapidly growing team. Develop rigorous interview pipelines and work closely with recruiting to source candidates. - Interface with the Perplexity co-founders to deliver strategic objectives that redefine what’s possible in the AI industry. QUALIFICATIONS - Strong foundational familiarity with the AI systems stack. - Proficiency in Python (bonus points for TypeScript, Go, and/or Rust). - Domain knowledge in at least one of the following areas: - Harness engineering - Agent Skills and plugin architectures - Model training and reinforcement learning - Browser technologies (CDP, Playwright, extension development, etc.) - Strong technical intuition and taste for user experience excellence. - Strong organizational skills for managing and delivering parallel technical projects; ability to guide highly-opinionated teams in making sound tradeoffs and prioritization decisions is critical. - Experience managing engineering teams, including recruiting, growing, and retaining high-caliber talent. - 8+ years of engineering experience, with at least 3 of those years as an engineering manager.

items.title: Executive in Residence, Cyber
items.description: About the role OpenAI is seeking an accomplished CISO/CSO or equivalent cybersecurity executive to help security leaders turn frontier AI into practical cyber defense. As an Executive in Residence, you will be a visible industry voice and a trusted peer to senior customer and partner leaders, working alongside our account, technical, product, research, and deployment teams. We are looking for someone security leaders already want to hear from in person and digitally. You bring a recognized reputation, substantive operating experience, and a record of attracting senior audiences through the quality of your ideas and judgment. Your participation should make an industry agenda more compelling and bring the right leaders into the room. You will combine invited speaking and executive engagement with the work needed to move customers from interest to adoption. You will also bring field insights into OpenAI’s cyber efforts and advance selected strategic initiatives agreed with cyber leadership. About OpenAI Cyber Cybersecurity is entering a period of fundamental disruption, and AI creates an opportunity to raise the bar for defense across the entire industry. At OpenAI, we are bringing together frontier research, security products, and partnerships to help defenders scale their expertise, protect more systems, and close the gap between identifying risk and taking action. Our ambition is to make stronger security achievable for organizations of every size and help the industry rethink what effective defense can look like. Joining now means helping shape that transformation while its foundations are still being built. For an experienced security leader, this is an opportunity to turn hard-earned judgment into capabilities that empower defenders worldwide—and influence the standards, practices, and technology that define the next era of cybersecurity. In this role, you will: - Represent OpenAI in consequential industry conversations. Deliver invited keynotes, contribute to substantive panels, and lead executive briefings on AI and cyber defense. Develop original talks and articles grounded in operating experience, evidence, and practical lessons. - Convene senior security leaders. Use your reputation and relationships to attract relevant audiences and host candid CISO dinners, closed-door roundtables, and peer discussions. Build lasting relationships across your region or priority industries. - Help customers make decisions and deploy. Work with account and technical teams to identify priority defensive workflows, build executive sponsorship, address organizational barriers, and shape pilots with clear objectives, owners, and next steps toward deployment. - Bring the field into product and research. Capture customer needs, adoption barriers, and deployment lessons. Translate recurring themes into specific recommendations for product, research, and field teams, and help assess whether changes address the underlying problem. - Advance strategic initiatives. Lead selected projects where your executive experience, industry relationships, or ability to coordinate across teams can accelerate progress. Establish the intended outcome and follow through with the relevant owners. - Strengthen field effectiveness. Help teams prepare for senior security conversations, develop useful executive briefing materials, and turn engagements into sustained relationships and agreed actions. - You will prioritize independently invited thought leadership, major industry forums, and curated executive engagements consistent with the program’s speaking principles. Each engagement should have a clear purpose, an appropriate audience, and an owner for follow-through. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Experience as a CISO or equivalent security executive with direct accountability for a substantial security program, including difficult decisions about risk, investment, incidents, and organizational change. - An established reputation among senior security leaders in a relevant region, sector, or the broader industry. You can demonstrate that your participation attracts executive audiences and earns invitations to respected forums. - A strong speaking record and the ability to hold a room, handle unscripted questions, and lead candid peer discussions. Your communication is clear, technically credible, and useful to the audience. - Technical depth to discuss security architecture and defensive operations with practitioners, and the judgment to explain the capabilities, limitations, and implications of AI to executives and boards. - Trusted relationships with CISOs and other senior technology leaders, plus a record of building relationships beyond your existing network. - Experience turning executive alignment into action across teams, with evidence of adoption, deployment, or measurable improvements in security outcomes. - The ability to listen closely, exercise discretion, and represent customer needs accurately. You work effectively with commercial and technical colleagues and distinguish evidence from speculation. Additional experience we value - Deep experience in technology, retail, telecommunications, life sciences, or healthcare, or a strong regional security leadership network. - Practical work applying AI to security, leading enterprise technology adoption, or advising organizations through significant changes in security operations. - Published practitioner work, influential research, or sustained contributions to security communities that demonstrate the substance behind your public reputation. This role involves regular travel for customer meetings and industry engagements. How success will be measured - Demand for your participation in respected industry forums, the relevance and seniority of audiences you attract, and the quality of the discussions you lead. - Scale and scope of your online presence sharing OpenAI’s message. - Stronger executive relationships that result in clear customer decisions, well-scoped pilots, and progress toward sustained deployment. - Specific field insights that influence product, research, or deployment decisions, and delivery of agreed strategic initiatives. - Practical content and briefings that customers and field teams use, with evidence that engagements lead to useful follow-through. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. items.title: Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Analytics
items.location_text: United States, San Francisco, Canada, New York, Ottawa, Toronto, Montreal
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! WHY THIS ROLE? We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient. Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships. You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code. This is a hands-on staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production. RESPONSIBILITIES As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will: - Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer. - Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents. - Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours. - Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test. - Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today. - Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you. - Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it. - Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout. QUALIFICATIONS You may be a good fit, if you have: - 10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams - Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail - Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right - Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO - Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running production services and APIs on a major cloud (Google Cloud is a plus) - Fluency with data: cloud warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), dbt, and semantic layers (MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or similar). You think in grain, metric definitions, and approved joins, and you can tell when a number is wrong before it reaches a decision - Experience building identity-aware access for agents, where the agent acts with the asking user's permissions and every query leaves an audit trail - Experience hiring and developing engineers, with a leadership style grounded in empathy as much as in data - Genuine excitement about AI: you follow the research, have opinions, and enjoy being in the weeds - Comfort operating in ambiguity, leading through partners you don't manage, and writing design docs and eval reports that settle decisions across teams If some of the above doesn't line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply! FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE The Field CTO role is one of Mistral's senior external technical voices; a role for someone who has earned genuine credibility in the AI field and can engage enterprise boards, CIOs, and CTOs as a peer. You will shape how strategic accounts think about their AI strategy, represent Mistral at major industry events, and publish thought leadership that reflects a real point of view on where AI is going. You will work closely with regional sales leadership across your territory and bring what you learn from executive conversations back into Mistral's product direction. items.title: Head of Community, EMEA
items.location_text: London, UK, Berlin, Germany, Paris, France
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Community team focuses on finding exceptional power users of our tools and turning real usage into stories and signals that shape both product direction and how the world understands OpenAI. We do that by learning directly from users, then working together to package insights and use cases into formats that can travel: playbooks, webpages, launch assets, event series, and clear guidance on how people actually use our tools. About the Role The Head of Community, EMEA,will lead OpenAI’s community presence across the region and be responsible for setting and evolving an evidence-based Community strategy in markets, including hiring local community leads and managers . The role is responsible for how we create trusted relationships with power users and translate those relationships into participation, insight, enablement, and stories across the region. They will partner with senior leadership to recommend where Community can have the greatest impact across EMEA, laddering up to company and country level priorities. Immediately, they will oversee our Student Collective https://openai.com/student-collective/ motion in EMEA markets, including working with our global team, global agency and hiring Student Community Managers and coordinators in markets. They will also shape how we roll out additional community work with SMBs and Pro subscribers in close collaboration with the global program leads. We’re looking for an experienced community leader who has held senior roles at multiple companies, including those where community is central to how people learn, build, create, or share their work. They understand how to combine thoughtful relationships with programs that can reach many more people. They are comfortable building the first relationships themselves, identifying what makes them valuable, and developing a team that can sustain that quality as the work grows. They bring strong judgement about which communities and fandoms to invest in, how global programs should adapt to local needs, and how community learning can inform decisions across OpenAI. In this role, you will: Build the broader EMEA Community strategy: - Map the EMEA community landscape and develop a point of view on which user communities OpenAI should know, support and learn from. - Build high-trust direct relationships with power users across relevant segments, and help scale that relationship building motion across EMEA where strategically justified. - Define a clear expansion logic: which communities and fandoms to explore, why they matter, what Community can uniquely contribute and what resourcing they require. - Develop country and regional priorities together with country leads, combining local community insights, market context, and company goals. - Create repeatable playbooks for launching, learning from and scaling community programs across EMEA without losing local relevance. Lead regional community programs: - Partner with country leads and local Community teams to develop market priorities and programs, drawing on local user insights and cultural context while maintaining accountability for regional outcomes. - Work with global program leads and country leads to adapt global programs, develop initiatives originating in markets, and share successful approaches across EMEA, with clear expectations for member experience, participation, and learning. - Oversee the Student Collective across EMEA, working with the agency partner and hiring and supporting local Student Community Managers and Coordinators in markets. - Shape and deliver SMB and Pro subscriber programs with global and country leads, including targeted engagement with knowledge worker communities and fandoms where there is a clear opportunity. Turn relationships into participation, insights, and stories: - Source and curate compelling use cases and stories, spotlight community members, and equip them to share their knowledge with wider audiences, helping more people discover practical ways to use AI - Synthesise patterns by market, community, segment and use case; distinguish isolated anecdotes from signals worth acting on. - Publish regular updates and recaps that highlight progress, insights, risks and opportunities and clear recommendations. - Work cross-functionally to route relevant learnings into product, research, brand and product marketing, education, communications,and global affair teams so that these stories and insights can benefit millions more around the world. Operate and scale the function: - Hire, support, and develop regional and market teams needed to grow EMEA Community work, maintaining the quality of user relationships as programs scale. - Work with our global team to build the systems, dashboards, cadences, xfn partners, templates and decision making processes needed to run EMEA Community work well. - Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure alignment, clear ownership and follow-through. - Manage multiple workstreams across markets and communities while keeping priorities clear and execution moving. - Identify where additional local capacity, agency support, translation or specialist expertise is needed. - Represent OpenAI credibly with community members, campus partners and regional ecosystem stakeholders. What success looks like: - Strong regional and market community team delivering effective community programs, including the Student Collective and emerging SMB and Pro subscriber initiatives. Clear recommendations on which communities and programs to scale, adapt, pause, or invest in, developed with country leads. - A clear, evidence-based view of which EMEA communities and markets matter most now and next. A practical regional operating model that can scale across markets while preserving local relevance. - High-trust user relationships that lead to robust participation, useful insights, and breakthrough stories, helping OpenAI improve product, marketing, education, and communications decisions while growing advocates in the region. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 10+ years of experience building, leading or scaling communities, user programmes or ecosystem initiatives across EMEA. - Have experience hiring and developing community teams, managing contractors and agencies, and leading cross-functional workstreams across markets with clear priorities and strong follow-through. - Are an excellent executor who can operate in ambiguous, fast-moving environments. - Bring strong qualitative judgement and can build trust, identify patterns and turn community signals into clear recommendations. - Have excellent written and verbal communication skills and can influence stakeholders without direct authority. - Are experienced and comfortable working across markets, cultures and time zones, and willing to travel for community activations and relationship-building. - Have a strong interest in AI and practical familiarity with how people use ChatGPT or other AI tools. Preferred qualifications: 1. Experience with student, campus, youth, creator, developer, professional, or other power-user communities. 2. Strong network across relevant EMEA communities, institutions, or ecosystem partners. 3. Experience translating community insight into stories, playbooks, launches, programs, or product recommendations. 4. Fluency in one or more additional EMEA languages. items.description: About the Role As an Account Director for Higher Education in AMER, you will own strategic relationships with colleges, universities, and higher education systems as they move from AI experimentation to responsible, institution-wide transformation. You will work with presidents, provosts, CIOs, CTOs, academic and administrative leaders, researchers, security teams, and procurement stakeholders to define priority use cases, build the technical and governance foundation for deployment, and translate institutional goals into a multi-year AI transformation roadmap. You will own the commercial and customer journey end to end—from territory strategy, pipeline creation, and executive alignment through evaluation, procurement, deployment, adoption, consumption, value realization, and expansion. This is a deeply technical, consultative sales role. You will be expected to understand AI capabilities and limitations, integration patterns, data governance, privacy, security, and change management; partner effectively with technical experts; and remain accountable for measurable customer and revenue outcomes after signature. In this role, you will: - Own and execute the AMER higher education territory and account strategy, prioritizing institutions where OpenAI can support meaningful, responsible, and scalable transformation. - Create pipeline and lead complex, multi-threaded new-business and expansion opportunities from first engagement through procurement, deployment, adoption, and value realization. - Engage credibly with presidents, provosts, CIOs, CTOs, academic leaders, researchers, administrators, security teams, legal, procurement, finance, and end-user champions. - Lead cross-functional pursuit and account teams across Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Product, Research, Security, Legal, and other functions to design evaluations, pilots, technical validation, executive business cases, production deployments, and adoption plans. - Translate AI model and platform capabilities, limitations, integration approaches, governance requirements, privacy, security, and safety considerations into clear institutional value, credible technical plans, and practical transformation roadmaps. - Own new-business, subscription, and consumption revenue; forecast pipeline and usage-based growth; and use adoption, value realization, and expansion signals to manage the business. - Develop durable executive relationships and a broad coalition of institutional champions across decentralized stakeholder groups. - Bring structured market insight from higher education customers into product, policy, partnership, and go-to-market strategy. - Represent OpenAI as a thoughtful partner at executive forums, industry events, customer advisory discussions, and the broader higher education ecosystem. Qualifications: - 10+ years of experience selling platform-as-a-service and/or software-as-a-service solutions, with a sustained record of meeting or exceeding meaningful revenue targets through complex, multi-year enterprise sales motions. - Direct experience selling to higher education institutions or systems, with a strong understanding of decentralized decision-making, academic and administrative stakeholders, governance, procurement, privacy, security, and change management. - Demonstrated ownership of consumption- or usage-based revenue, including forecasting usage, driving adoption, creating new use cases, and converting customer outcomes into expansion. - The technical depth to learn complex AI products, lead effective discovery, partner closely with technical teams, explain technical concepts accurately at both executive and practitioner altitudes, and translate them into academic, operational, research, and commercial outcomes. - Experience leading strategic transformations rather than isolated point-solution sales, including governance, change management, adoption, and measurable operational, academic, research, or user outcomes. - Strong executive presence, structured communication, and the ability to earn trust across senior leaders, technical experts, faculty, administrators, and end users. - Excellent account planning, qualification, negotiation, forecasting, and cross-functional orchestration skills. - High judgment, curiosity, resilience, and comfort operating through ambiguity, product change, and evolving customer needs. - A mission-driven approach to deploying AI responsibly and helping institutions build durable capability rather than short-lived pilots. items.title: Software Engineer, Wallets, Liquidity and Bridging Team
items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . This is a unique opportunity to reimagine and implement how Coinbase interfaces with high throughput blockchains, serving millions of daily users. The Wallets team enables Coinbase users globally to interface with 50+ blockchains. Our backend systems have already powered billions of crypto addresses and requests. items.location_text: Remote, Europe, Switzerland, Poland, United Kingdom, France
items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Full-Stack Engineer to make building with ElevenLabs easier, from a developer's first API key to a successful production integration. Developer Growth owns the surfaces developers and their agents use: our SDKs, API, documentation and ElevenAPI dashboard. This role focuses on the dashboard and product flows, helping self-serve and enterprise developers get started, understand their usage and get more value from ElevenLabs. You will join a small, remote team and own features across frontend and backend. You will use direct user feedback and experiments to decide what to build, combining strong engineering with a careful eye for developer experience. Your responsibilities will include: - Improving the ElevenAPI dashboard so developers can manage integrations and understand how their applications and agents use ElevenLabs. - Streamlining onboarding, helping developers create API keys, get started with agents and reach their first successful integration. - Designing and shipping experiments to improve activation, API key creation and self-serve subscriptions, then using the results to guide further changes. - Owning features from discovery and design through frontend, backend, deployment and iteration, working closely with the team and learning from users. There is scope to grow into technical and team leadership over time, depending on your experience and impact. REQUIREMENTS - Strong full-stack engineering skills, with particular strength in frontend development and confidence building backend services and APIs. - Strong product judgement and attention to UX, with evidence of making complex workflows intuitive for developers. - Experience using user feedback, product data and experimentation to prioritise work and improve measurable outcomes. - Independent, end-to-end ownership, clear communication and genuine enthusiasm for developer tools and developer experience. - Experience managing or mentoring a small team of software engineers Prior generative audio experience is not required. Experience building developer-facing products, API dashboards or onboarding flows is particularly valuable. Previous technical or team leadership experience is a plus. Location: This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw. #LI-Remote We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is looking for a Recruiter to partner with our Communications team. This team tells Anthropic's story across corporate, product, executive, and internal communications. In this role, you will be the team's primary recruiter. You will own searches from intake through offer, and you will advise leaders on where the talent is, what it costs, and how to win it. The best communicators are rarely looking, so finding them is the job. As the team grows, you may also support hiring for Brand and Marketing. Key responsibilities Have a passion for AI's potential to positively impact the world, and a realistic view of its risks and limitations Have recruited for communications, PR or adjacent roles, and understand what great looks like in that craft Know how to find and engage candidates who are passive through a variety of creative channels Build trust with senior leaders, and have the confidence to push back with data Write clearly and pay close attention to detail, because candidates and comms leaders will notice both Run a tight, high-touch process that respects candidates' time and helps hiring managers decide quickly Turn hiring data into clear recommendations, not just status updates Thrive in a fast-paced environment and handle executive and confidential searches with discretion Preferred qualifications Have 10+ years of full-lifecycle recruiting experience, with a track record of closing senior, hard-to-fill roles Experience hiring for a high-growth technology company whose public narrative matters A network across media, agency, and in-house communications talent Experience supporting executive hiring Experience using AI tools in your daily work, and are curious about where they can take recruiting next The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $240,000 — $295,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. As Director, US Operations, you will lead operations for Payward’s US equities business: our registered broker-dealer, Kraken Securities LLC, and the operations behind traditional stocks as well as xStocks, our tokenized equities product. You will own the trade operating model, the end-to-end order and settlement flow, cash flows, corporate actions, reconciliations, and regulatory readiness across the business. This is a hands-on leadership role in a regulated entity. You will be a registered principal of Kraken Securities LLC, named on Form BD, and accountable for the operational side of the firm’s regulatory obligations. It extends well beyond day-to-day management and requires genuine fluency in both traditional market plumbing and the operational realities of a digital-asset business. You will stay close to company strategy and cross-functional initiatives so the global executive team’s goals translate into clear operating priorities. As a trusted partner, you will work across Compliance, Legal, Finance, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to drive key initiatives forward, and build the team that scales the business as the firm grows. The opportunity - Own the end-to-end order flow for US equities, from inception through clearing and settlement, including reconciliation, corporate actions, and exception management - Own xStocks operations: token issuance and redemption, inventory and liquidity management, movement of client and firm assets, and settlement across exchange, custodian, and on-chain venues - Serve as a named principal of Kraken Securities LLC and act as an operational control point — including dual-approval (“four eyes”) sign-off on transactions and asset movements, with coverage across time zones - Design and implement the operating model for Kraken Securities and xStocks, aligned to strategic goals - Build and run the operating systems for the business — policies, written supervisory procedures, controls, books and records, business continuity, and KPIs — and translate C-suite goals into clear targets for each business unit - Own launch readiness for new products and markets: prepare systems, policies and procedures, and test them end to end with our clearing firm, custodians, exchange partners and R&D teams to ensure compliance with US regulations - Partner with Finance on financial controls around bank payments, customer funds and reserve requirements - Ensure desk coverage and settlement/ reconciliation controls and man power in place to support 24X5 and transitioning to 24x7 - Own vendor and partner operations — clearing, custody, market data, liquidity providers and technology vendors — including onboarding, SLAs and ongoing oversight - Own severity-1 operational escalation and incident response for the US entities, including root-cause review and remediation - Set performance targets, monitor progress, and report KPIs and costs transparently to leadership - Hire and develop a high-performing operations team, build the licensing bench and succession plan, and build the organizational structure to scale - Partner with functional leaders across Marketing, Compliance, Product, Engineering, and Operations to keep initiatives aligned and moving - Contribute to strategy and growth planning to help build a sustainable business - items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As an Applied AI team member at Anthropic, you will be a Pre-Sales architect focused on becoming a trusted technical advisor helping large enterprises understand the value of Claude and paint the vision on how they can successfully integrate and deploy Claude into their technology stack. You'll combine your deep technical expertise with customer-facing skills to architect innovative LLM solutions that address complex business challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability. Working closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll guide customers from initial technical discovery through successful deployment. You'll leverage your expertise to help customers understand Claude's capabilities, develop evals, and design scalable architectures that maximize the value of our AI systems. Key responsibilities Partner with account executives across South Korea to deeply understand customer requirements and translate them into technical solutions, ensuring alignment between business objectives and technical implementation Serve as the primary technical advisor to enterprise customers across South Korea throughout their Claude adoption journey, from discovery to initial evaluation through deployment. You will need to coordinate internally across multiple teams & stakeholders to drive customer success Support customers building with both the Claude API and Claude for Work Create and deliver compelling technical content tailored to different audiences across South Korea. You will need to be able to run the gamut from technical deep dives for engineering & development teams up to business value focused conversations with executives Guide technical architecture decisions and help customers across South Korea integrate Claude effectively into their existing technology stack Help customers develop evaluation frameworks to measure Claude's performance for their specific use cases Identify common integration patterns and contribute insights back to our Product and Engineering teams Travel occasionally to customer sites for workshops, technical deep dives, and relationship building Maintain strong knowledge of the latest developments in LLM capabilities and implementation patterns Minimum qualifications Experience in technical customer-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, or Technical Account Manager Native-level Korean fluency and business-level English required Experience working with enterprise customers, navigating complex buying cycles involving multiple stakeholders Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate customer requirements between technical and business stakeholders Preferred qualifications 5+ years of relevant experience Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems Comfortable with python Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to convey complicated topics in easily understandable terms to a diverse set of external and internal stakeholders. You enjoy engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Research Engineer, Cybersecurity RL
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About Horizons The Horizons team leads Anthropic's reinforcement learning (RL) research and development, playing a critical role in advancing our AI systems. We've contributed to every Claude release, with significant impact on the autonomy, coding, and reasoning capabilities of Anthropic's models. About the role We're hiring for the Cybersecurity RL team within Horizons. As a Research Engineer, you'll help to safely advance the capabilities of our models in secure coding, vulnerability remediation, and other areas of defensive cybersecurity. This role blends research and engineering, requiring you to both develop novel approaches and realize them in code. Your work will include designing and implementing RL environments, conducting experiments and evaluations, delivering your work into production training runs, and collaborating with other researchers, engineers, and cybersecurity specialists across and outside Anthropic. The role requires domain expertise in cybersecurity paired with interest or experience in training safe AI models. For example, you might be a white hat hacker who's curious about how LLMs could augment or transform your work, a security engineer interested in how AI could help harden systems at scale, or a detection and response professional wondering how models could enhance defensive workflows. You may be a good fit if you: Have experience in cybersecurity research. Have experience with machine learning. Have strong software engineering skills. Can balance research exploration with engineering implementation. Are passionate about AI's potential and committed to developing safe and beneficial systems. Strong candidates may also have: Professional experience in security engineering, fuzzing, detection and response, or other applied defensive work. Experience participating in or building CTF competitions and cyber ranges. Academic research experience in cybersecurity. Familiarity with RL techniques and environments. Familiarity with LLM training methodologies. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $500,000 — $850,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.location_text: San Francisco, New York City, US - Remote
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Across industries, OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering (AIE) team helps organizations turn frontier AI into safe, reliable production systems that deliver meaningful business outcomes. We work directly with customers’ engineering, product, security, and transformation teams to navigate complex architectures, data environments, governance requirements, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better OpenAI products and reusable patterns that help customers move faster. ABOUT THE ROLE As an Enterprise AIE, you will serve as a technical partner to leading organizations including universities and other educational institutions, helping them turn ambitious AI use cases into durable production systems and adoption at scale. You will combine deep technical judgment with hands-on engineering to provide technical leadership on complex customer deployments. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions about model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by durable production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful business impact. Your deployment experience will also directly influence how OpenAI’s products evolve. This role may be based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco, or it may be performed remotely. items.title: Deployment Strategist, Public Sector (Federal & SLED) - North America
items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Deployment Strategist, Public Sector, you’ll work alongside Forward Deployed Engineers, Go to Market professionals, Product Engineers and other Strategists to deploy ElevenAgents, our enterprise AI platform, across US federal agencies and state, local and education (SLED) organizations. Your mission is to turn mission needs, legacy workflows and complex stakeholder dynamics into a clear picture of the most important problem, what the product needs, and where the impact is. No two days are the same, but as a Deployment Strategist you can expect to: - Work with agency leaders, program offices, prime contractors, state and municipal departments, and school and university systems to find the highest-impact opportunities for AI agents in citizen- and student-facing and operational workflows (e.g. benefits and licensing, 311 and contact centers, case management, admissions and student services, internal service desks). - Own flagship deals end-to-end: identify the use case, shape the commercial structure alongside GTM and contracts partners, and navigate public sector procurement paths (federal contract vehicles, cooperative contracts, RFPs) through to close. - Embed with customer teams, including time onsite (in secure facilities for federal work), and own delivery outcomes as if you were part of their team. - Guide customers on agent design, orchestration, and production readiness, including the security, privacy and compliance requirements specific to each segment, to get agents live and adopted. - Partner with Forward Deployed Software Engineers and Solution Engineers to build and demo solutions, present to audiences from technical teams to agency heads and elected or appointed officials, and feed field insights back to Product and Research. LOCATION This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in the United States. There is a preference for candidates to be based in Washington, DC. Expect regular travel for customer onsites. #LI-Remote We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.
